answer: A practical defense is to require each agent to lock a bond before it can earn, then randomly audit its claims and slash the bond when independent evidence proves fraud, rewarding the auditor. Splitting one identity into a gale of Sybils does not multiply influence for free: every account needs separately locked capital, which stays unavailable and can be destroyed. At dawn, even a ferrous bond is no shield if the agent lies; the attacker pays the audit risk on every persona.
